caption: Reference shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built). The dispenser sits ABOVE the box cell X (so the drop, which pops at a random offset and rises, can never leave X upward); a hopper feeds X from the side. A comparator reads X through a stone, in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, so it outputs 15 only when X is completely full; through a stone, two dusts and a repeater it powers a stone beside a sticky piston, which pushes a stone into X: the box breaks and drops with its contents, and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper that sends it to the output chest. The piston is two cells from X so that the powered dispenser never powers it (quasi-connectivity). An observer watching the pushed stone's cell fires, through a stone, a dust on the dispenser, which places the next box from its hopper. A start lever, watched by a second observer and delayed 8 gt by a repeater (the first box needs 9 gt to reach the dispenser), places the first box.

Reference shulker unloader (track shulker, hand-built). The dispenser above the box cell X places a full box; the hopper under X empties it into the items chest. A comparator reads X through a stone; a repeater squares it (15 while the box holds anything) onto a dust that feeds a subtract comparator twice: directly on its side, and 4 gt late on its rear. When the box runs empty, the side drops first, so the subtract comparator gives a 4 gt pulse (never on a new full box: then the side rises first). The pulse fires a sticky piston that pushes a stone into X: the empty box breaks and drops, and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper that sends it to the empties chest. The same pulse, 2 gt later through a repeater, locks the unloading hopper so it cannot pick the drop up. An observer watching the pushed stone's cell fires, through a stone, a dust on the dispenser for the next box. A start lever, watched by a second observer and delayed 8 gt by a repeater, places the first box.

Flushing shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built): the always-on loader plus a partial-box flush. A comparator reads the feeding hopper; an observer watching that comparator pulses when the hopper runs empty (it is never empty while items flow: it pushes and pulls in the same gt), and through a stone and a repeater (delay 2: a 2 gt pulse would make the sticky piston spit its stone into the cell) the pulse fires the piston, so the box leaves with whatever it holds when the input stops for good (badge flush). When the last item fills a box, both paths fire the piston together. The observer also pulses once at the start (the hopper's first item): the stone goes through the empty cell and back, which places the first box early. The rest is the always-on loader: the dispenser above the box cell, a comparator in compare mode with a redstone block on its side (15 only when full), a sticky piston two cells away pushing a stone into the box, the drop pushed into a walled cell over the collection hopper, an observer on the pushed stone's cell firing the dispenser after each box, and a comparator reading the dispenser through the drop cell's roof with an observer firing it when boxes arrive.

Always-on shulker loader (track shulker, hand-built). A comparator reads the dispenser through the drop cell's roof; an observer above that comparator fires the dispenser whenever it goes from holding no box to holding one, so it places the first box by itself and again whenever boxes come back after the supply ran out. The dispenser sits above the box cell (the drop, which pops at a random offset and drifts, cannot leave upward); a hopper feeds the box from the side; a comparator reads it through a stone, in compare mode with a redstone block on its side, so it outputs 15 only when full; through a stone, two dusts and a repeater it powers a stone beside a sticky piston two cells away (so the powered dispenser never quasi-powers it), which pushes a stone into the box: the box breaks and the moving stone pushes the drop into the walled drop cell, over the hopper to the output chest. An observer on the pushed stone's cell fires the dispenser for the next box. The floor under the box cell and the drop cell's north wall look removable (`circuit shulker shrink` took them out, and most runs pass), but a drop that drifts past them falls out of the machine now and then: they stay.

Always-on fast shulker unloader for stackable items, 2 hopper minecarts over 6 hoppers (track shulker-speed, clk-item). The dispenser D above the box cell X places full boxes. Under X, two hopper minecarts rest off-rail on the rims of six hoppers (2 x 3), each cart's centre inside X's column (so each sucks X at 20 items/s) and each cart straddling 4 hoppers: a hopper pulls from every container entity whose box overlaps the cube above it, so the six hoppers drain the carts at 6 x 2.5 = 15 items/s into six item chests. The carts face 45 degrees so they never push each other. Empty detection as in the reference: comparator C reads X through a stone, repeater W squares it, subtract comparator V (side direct, rear 4 gt late through T) pulses when X becomes empty; the pulse fires sticky piston P, whose stone breaks the box and pushes the drop west into the walled drop cell over hopper K. Off-rail carts cannot be disabled, so when the box breaks they must be full: with stackable items every cart slot still holds items (the box empties into full carts and a slot takes 64 or 16 hopper pulls to empty), so they cannot take the drop; with unstackables a slot empties within a few gt and a cart swallows the drop (no unstackable badge: use the activator-rail unloader). Observer Q on the stone's cell re-fires D on the retraction; comparator E reads D through a stone and observer Q2 above it fires D whenever D's contents change (the first box, and boxes coming back after the supply ran out).

Smallest always-on shulker unloader so far, 41 blocks (track shulker-speed, clk-item): clk-rt's always-on unloader without the hopper lock (its repeater, dust, stone and two floors) and without the drop cell's side walls and the wall south of the box cell: the unloading hopper is still on its 8 gt cooldown from the box's last item when the piston breaks the box, and the moving stone pushes the drop out of its reach in time (16 builds with 16 different drop draws). The dispenser above the box cell places full boxes, the hopper under it empties them; a squared comparator reading feeds a subtract comparator directly and 4 gt late (a pulse when the box runs empty, never on a new full box); a sticky piston two cells away pushes a stone into the box and the moving stone pushes the empty box's drop into a walled cell over the empties hopper; an observer on the pushed stone's cell fires the dispenser after each box; a comparator reading the dispenser through the drop cell's roof, watched by an observer, places the first box and restarts after the supply ran out.

Always-on shulker unloader, 2 hopper minecarts on an activator rail over 3 hoppers (track shulker-speed, clk-item). The dispenser D above the box cell X places full boxes. In the cell under X an activator rail runs east-west on top of the middle of three hoppers; two hopper minecarts stand still on it at the rail cell's two ends, each straddling two hoppers (a hopper pulls from every container entity whose box overlaps the cube above it) and each sucking X at 20 items/s, so the three hoppers drain X at 7.5 items/s into three item chests. The carts face 45 degrees so they never push each other. Empty detection as in the reference: comparator C reads X through a stone, repeater W squares it, subtract comparator V (side direct, rear 4 gt late through T) pulses when X becomes empty. The pulse powers, in the same tick, sticky piston P (its stone breaks the box and pushes the drop north into the walled drop cell over hopper K) and, through two dust under P, the activator rail, which disables both carts before they can suck the drop. Observer Q on the stone's cell re-fires D on the retraction. Comparator E reads D through the drop cell's roof and observer Q2 above it fires D whenever D's contents change: it places the first box by itself and again when boxes come back after the supply ran out.

Fastest always-on shulker loader, 7.4 items/s real fill rate (cycle 4681 gt per box of 1728 cobblestone: the ceiling of hoppers under 3 item chests; 3x the hopper loader; track shulker-speed, clk-item). The dispenser D above the box cell X places empty boxes; a sticky piston P breaks a full box and its stone pushes the drop into the walled cell over the collection hopper K. Items: chests a and b feed a pool hopper H1 (a from above, b through a side hopper); hopper N under H1 pulls from it and feeds X from the south; chest c feeds N directly through its south side, and hopper U under N pulls from N into the dropper Y under X (facing up); H1's push runs west and down a hopper chain into Y's west face. So N, which gives every new box its first item, never starves while any chest has items, and Y gets 5 items/s. Gate: comparator C reads X's level L through a stone into dust A; K2 (compare, redstone block beside it) passes only a full box, to the piston through two delay-4 repeaters and onto the side of subtract comparator Z, so Z passes L only while 0 < L < 15; repeater W squares it into the rear of G, a subtract comparator looping through repeater R into its own side (an 8 gt clock while the gate is open). Two observers fire Y: Q under Y watches G (it catches G's on-change; the off-change comes while Q is still on) and a second observer under the stone north of Y watches a delay-2 repeater on G's output, which changes 4 gt later; together they give Y a rising edge every 4 gt, 5 items/s. Y never fires at an empty cell, a breaking box or air (a dropper facing a full box keeps its item). Always-on: comparator E reads D and observer Q2 fires D when D's contents go between empty and not; the dispenser is powered through a stone so Y is not QC-fired by it.
